raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`apply_qk_norm`'s fused in-place path is CUDA-only. On ROCm, `q`/`k` fall back to `reshape(-1, head_dim)`, and because they are slices of the fused QKV output (row stride `(num_heads + 2 * num_kv_heads) * head_dim`, e.g. 6144 for Qwen3-8B), that reshape is a full copy in every layer. The JIT `qknorm` kernel takes per-tensor strides and handles this layout without a copy, but it did not build on ROCm.

## Modifications

- `qknorm.cuh`: drop the `cuda_bf16.h` / `cuda_fp16.h` includes. `sgl_kernel/utils.cuh`, already included, provides them on CUDA and the `hip_*` equivalents on ROCm, so the CUDA build is unchanged. #40585 makes the same change to this file.
- `apply_qk_norm`: enable the fused path on HIP. `can_use_fused_inplace_qknorm` still falls back to the existing path if the kernel cannot be built.
- `apply_qk_norm`: return early on zero tokens. An idle DP-attention rank reaches the fused path with an empty batch, where `q.view(batch_size, -1, head_dim)` cannot infer the head count. CUDA takes this path on `main` as well.
- `VisionAttention`: take the JIT QK-norm branch only at TP=1. InternViT-6B (InternVL2.5-26B, InternVL3-38B/78B) normalizes across all heads, and under TP the branch saw only the local heads and skipped `_apply_qk_norm`'s all-gather. At TP=1 it is unchanged.
- `test_qknorm.py`: run on AMD CI, add a packed-QKV test for both launchers and an empty-batch test for `apply_qk_norm`. The AOT comparison stays CUDA-only because its reference, `sgl_kernel.rmsnorm`, is not in the ROCm build.

The launchers' ROCm device check (`kDLGPU`) is on `main` since #47300.

On ROCm the launcher keeps the one-row-per-warp kernel; the head_dim-128 two-rows-per-warp variant from #45214 is CUDA-only.

Unlike #21734 (reverted in #23159), the strided view only goes to the JIT kernel; the AITER RMSNorm fallback still gets the contiguous 2-D tensor.

Affected models are those that call `apply_qk_norm` on ROCm: Qwen3-MoE (its fused QK-norm + RoPE is CUDA/XPU-only), dense Qwen3, `glm4_moe`, `bailing_moe`, `sdar`, `laguna` and others. For dense Qwen3 with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, decode already uses the aiter fused kernel from #44267, so only prefill and extend change. Llama 4 is unaffected: it calls `apply_qk_norm` only on CUDA.

## Accuracy Tests

Kernel on MI325X, built from this branch: for head_dim 64/128/256/512/1024 in bf16 and fp16, normalizing a strided fused-QKV slice gives bit-identical output to normalizing a contiguous copy, matches an fp32 reference (`atol=rtol=2e-2`), and leaves the V columns untouched. On `main`, the ROCm build fails (`'cuda_bf16.h' file not found`) and `can_use_fused_inplace_qknorm` returns `False`.

Kernel on MI355X, main `b960aa903a` with this PR: q/k views of a packed qkv for 10 per-rank geometries (Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-30B-A3B, Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen3-235B and GLM-4.5 at TP 8, head_dim 64 to 1024), 1 to 8192 tokens, bf16 and fp16, rows 16 B and 8 B aligned: 280 of 280 cases match a contiguous copy bit for bit and an fp32 reference (`atol=rtol=2e-2`) and leave V untouched, and the kernel replays correctly from a captured HIP graph. `apply_qk_norm` takes the fused path in place and matches the existing path within one bf16 ulp, with and without `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`.

On MI355X at `main` `1ced9a9eb0`, `test_qknorm.py` passes (8 tests; the AOT comparison is skipped). The empty-batch test fails without the early return.

GSM8K, Qwen3-8B, 5-shot, greedy, 500 questions:

| GPU | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| MI325X | 0.920 | 0.920 |
| MI355X | 0.932 | 0.934 |

GSM8K, Qwen3-30B-A3B, MI355X, `main` `1ced9a9eb0`, TP=1, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, 5-shot, greedy, all 1319 questions, `--disable-radix-cache`, six runs over two servers each:

| | Mean | Runs |
|---|---|---|
| Base | 0.911 | 0.911 / 0.911 / 0.910 / 0.911 / 0.908 / 0.914 |
| This PR | 0.908 | 0.902 / 0.907 / 0.910 / 0.908 / 0.916 / 0.906 |

The difference is within run-to-run noise (t ≈ 1.3).

InternVL3-38B, MI355X, TP=1: 24 of 24 graded image questions correct on both base and this PR, and identical captions for three images. For InternViT-6B's attention at TP 2 / 4 / 8, the vision JIT branch without the TP guard gives a max error of 0.22 / 0.47 / a launcher crash against the all-head norm.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Kernel.** bf16, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, per-call GPU time from graph replay on MI355X. `before` is the current ROCm path (copy + two AITER RMSNorm launches).

| Shape | Tokens | Before | This PR | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-8B 32q/8kv | 1024 | 23.3 us | 6.2 us | 3.76x |
| Qwen3-8B 32q/8kv | 8192 | 111.3 us | 34.6 us | 3.22x |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B 32q/4kv | 8192 | 99.2 us | 30.1 us | 3.30x |
| MHA 16q/16kv, head_dim 64 | 4096 | 46.4 us | 11.5 us | 4.04x |
| **Sum of 12 shapes** | | **640.5 us** | **182.7 us** | **3.51x** |

The copy accounts for 44% of the saving on MI355X and 29% on MI325X; the rest comes from replacing two norm launches with one.

**End to end.** MI325X, `python -m sglang.benchmark.offline_throughput`, random 1024 in / 128 out, `--disable-radix-cache`, TP=1, three alternating base/PR pairs:

| Model | Per-pair delta | Median |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-30B-A3B | +2.73 / +3.40 / +3.11 % | **+3.11 %** |
| Mistral-7B (no QK norm, control) | −0.21 / +1.23 / −0.38 % | −0.21 % |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

#### 1. 🔴 Blocking: ROCm tensors export as kDLROCM, failing kDLCUDA device check
`python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/elementwise/qknorm.cuh:126`

`QKNormKernelWarp::run` and `QKNormKernelCTA::run` restrict with `device.set_options<kDLCUDA>()`, but on ROCm tvm-ffi exports GPU tensors as `kDLROCM`, so `TensorMatcher.verify(q)` raises on every call. Since `can_use_fused_inplace_qknorm` only compiles and never runs, it returns True and no fallback occurs, crashing `apply_qk_norm` for Qwen3-style models. Use the `kDLGPU` alias.

**How it is reached:** launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-* on ROCm (default flags: SGLANG_USE_AITER unset, so every pass is native; with it set, prefill/extend is still native) -> Qwen3Attention.forward -> forward_prepare_native -> models/utils.py apply_qk_norm, whose gate (_is_cuda or _is_hip) is now true on HIP -> can_use_fused_inplace_qknorm (compile only, returns True for head_dim 64-1024) -> fused_inplace_qknorm -> module.qknorm -> QKNormKernelWarp/CTA::run, where device.set_options<kDLCUDA>() rejects the tensor because it arrives as kDLROCM

**Who is affected:** Every ROCm user serving a model that calls apply_qk_norm (Qwen3, Qwen3-MoE, Qwen3-Next, GLM4-MoE, Olmo2 and others) with default settings; it fails on the first forward pass.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

#### 2. 🟠 Should fix: No ROCm test or CI coverage for new default path
`test/registered/kernels/ops/layernorm/test_qknorm.py:10`

The PR turns on the fused JIT `fused_inplace_qknorm` path in `apply_qk_norm` for ROCm (about 30 call sites in 21 model files) but adds no ROCm test. `test_qknorm.py` registers only `register_cuda_ci`, tests only bf16, and compares against AOT `sgl_kernel.rmsnorm` / flashinfer. The one AMD-registered test that calls `apply_qk_norm` (`test_model_fast_paths.py`) skips that case off CUDA via `requires_inline_ptx`. As a result, ROCm correctness of the new default path, including fp16 and head_dim 512/1024, is never exercised in CI. Add `register_amd_ci` coverage with a torch reference such as `python/sglang/test/kernels/qknorm.py:torch_impl_qknorm`, like `test_rmsnorm.py` does.

**Who is affected:** ROCm users of any model that calls `apply_qk_norm` with head_dim in {64..1024}; a regression in the HIP build of the kernel would not be caught by CI.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

`python/sglang/srt/models/utils.py:514-530`

#### 1. 🔴 Blocking: ROCm tensors export as kDLROCM, failing kDLCUDA device check
`python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/elementwise/qknorm.cuh:126`

`QKNormKernelWarp::run` and `QKNormKernelCTA::run` restrict with `device.set_options<kDLCUDA>()`, but on ROCm tvm-ffi exports GPU tensors as `kDLROCM`, so `TensorMatcher.verify(q)` raises on every call. Since `can_use_fused_inplace_qknorm` only compiles and never runs, it returns True and no fallback occurs, crashing `apply_qk_norm` for Qwen3-style models. Use the `kDLGPU` alias.

**How it is reached:** launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-* on ROCm (default flags: SGLANG_USE_AITER unset, so every pass is native; with it set, prefill/extend is still native) -> Qwen3Attention.forward -> forward_prepare_native -> models/utils.py apply_qk_norm, whose gate (_is_cuda or _is_hip) is now true on HIP -> can_use_fused_inplace_qknorm (compile only, returns True for head_dim 64-1024) -> fused_inplace_qknorm -> module.qknorm -> QKNormKernelWarp/CTA::run, where device.set_options<kDLCUDA>() rejects the tensor because it arrives as kDLROCM

**Who is affected:** Every ROCm user serving a model that calls apply_qk_norm (Qwen3, Qwen3-MoE, Qwen3-Next, GLM4-MoE, Olmo2 and others) with default settings; it fails on the first forward pass.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

#### 2. 🟠 Should fix: No ROCm test or CI coverage for new default path
`test/registered/kernels/ops/layernorm/test_qknorm.py:10`

The PR turns on the fused JIT `fused_inplace_qknorm` path in `apply_qk_norm` for ROCm (about 30 call sites in 21 model files) but adds no ROCm test. `test_qknorm.py` registers only `register_cuda_ci`, tests only bf16, and compares against AOT `sgl_kernel.rmsnorm` / flashinfer. The one AMD-registered test that calls `apply_qk_norm` (`test_model_fast_paths.py`) skips that case off CUDA via `requires_inline_ptx`. As a result, ROCm correctness of the new default path, including fp16 and head_dim 512/1024, is never exercised in CI. Add `register_amd_ci` coverage with a torch reference such as `python/sglang/test/kernels/qknorm.py:torch_impl_qknorm`, like `test_rmsnorm.py` does.

**Who is affected:** ROCm users of any model that calls `apply_qk_norm` with head_dim in {64..1024}; a regression in the HIP build of the kernel would not be caught by CI.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

#### 1. 🟠 Should fix: Zero-token batch crashes forward pass on ROCm: this PR routes HIP through the fused QK norm path
`python/sglang/srt/models/utils.py:514-530`

With this PR, ROCm takes the fused path in `apply_qk_norm`, which calls `q.view(batch_size, -1, head_dim)`. For a 0-token batch that `view` raises `RuntimeError` ('-1 is ambiguous'). The base HIP fallback (`_reshape_for_qk_norm` -> `RMSNorm`, which skips empty input) handled this case. Even past the `view`, the launchers in `qknorm.cuh` would compute `num_blocks=0` with no zero-grid guard. The same `view` already sits on the CUDA path since #15835, so this extends an existing hazard to ROCm; add a `q.numel() == 0` early return, as #31794 did for `fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm`.

**Who is affected:** ROCm users serving models that call `apply_qk_norm` without an empty-batch guard (e.g. Qwen3 dense, Llama4, SDAR) when a rank runs a 0-token batch, such as an idle rank under DP attention.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**Related past reviews:** [#19059](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/19059) on `python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/elementwise/fused_qknorm_rope.cuh`
